title: Generate the first n squares
description: Write a generator function `first_n_squares(n)` that yields the squares `0, 1, 4, 9, ...` for each `i` in `range(n)`, i.e. it yields `i * i` for `i` from 0 up to (but not including) `n`.
hints: Instead of building and returning a whole list, this function should produce values one at a time as they are requested.
The `yield` keyword turns a function into a generator: each `yield expr` produces the next value of the sequence.
Loop with `for i in range(n):` and `yield i * i` inside the loop, rather than returning a list.
expected_behavior: A generator that, when iterated, produces i * i for each i in range(n), in increasing order of i.
explanation: Using `yield` inside the loop makes `first_n_squares` a generator function: calling it returns a generator object, and each iteration of the `for` loop over `range(n)` produces the next square `i * i` on demand, without ever materializing the full list in memory.
